Workshop 5 · Practice problems

Which item matches best?

Work these out by hand, without running code, the way the exam works. Total 20 marks. The log values you need are given; a calculator helps with square roots.

Print

Problems 1, 2 and 4 to 6 use this small menu of four items:

D1  tea with milk     D2  coffee with milk     D3  tea with lemon     D4  cake with cream

The vocabulary, in this order, is cake, coffee, cream, lemon, milk, tea, with. Use log₁₀ 1 = 0, log₁₀ 2 = 0.30, log₁₀ 4 = 0.60.

  1. [2]

    Write the count vectors of D1 and of the query "tea with cream", in the order of the vocabulary.

  2. [3]

    With the count vectors, work out the cosine similarity of the query "tea with cream" with each of D1 to D4. Which items come first?

  3. [2]

    (a) Work out the cosine of [2, 1, 0] and [1, 1, 1]. (b) What is the cosine of [1, 2] and [2, 4], and why?

  4. [3]

    Work out the df and the idf of every word in the vocabulary. N = 4.

  5. [4]

    With TF-IDF weights, work out the cosine of the query "tea with cream" with D1 and with D4. Show the dot product and both lengths.

  6. [2]

    In problem 5, TF-IDF puts cake with cream above tea with milk for the query "tea with cream". Explain why. Is that what the customer wanted?

  7. [2]

    Why does a search engine use cosine similarity rather than just the dot product? Give an example.

  8. [2]

    A customer searches for "chai". The menu has tea with milk but no item with the word chai. What cosine does TF-IDF give tea with milk, and why? What kind of method would do better?

Answers will be released on the Workshop 5 page after class.
